content: 1. For hematogenous osteomyelitis where MRSA is unlikely, the preferred treatment regimen includes either Nafcillin at a dose of 37 mg/kg administered intravenously every 6 hours (with a maximum daily dose of 8–12 g) or Oxacillin at the same dosage and frequency. If Gram-negative bacilli are identified on Gram stain, it is recommended to add either Ceftazidime at 50 mg/kg IV every 8 hours or Cefepime at 150 mg/kg/day IV divided every 8 hours. 2. For hematogenous osteomyelitis caused by MRSA, the preferred regimen is Vancomycin at 1 g IV every 12 hours. An alternative regimen includes Linezolid at 600 mg IV or orally every 12 hours, with or without Rifampin at 300 mg orally or IV twice daily. 3. In cases of contiguous osteomyelitis with vascular insufficiency, it is essential to debride the overlying ulcer and send a bone specimen for histological examination and culture. Empiric antimicrobial therapy should not be initiated unless the patient is acutely ill. Antibiotic therapy should be guided by culture results, and the treatment duration should be at least 6 weeks. Revascularization should be performed if feasible. 4. For open fracture osteomyelitis involving long bones after internal fixation, the following regimens are recommended: If caused by S. aureus or P. aeruginosa, the preferred regimen is Vancomycin at 1 g IV every 12 hours combined with either Ceftazidime at 2 g IV every 8 hours or Cefepime at 2 g IV every 8 hours. Alternative regimens include Linezolid at 600 mg IV or orally twice daily combined with either Ceftazidime at 2 g IV every 8 hours or Cefepime at 2 g IV every 8 hours. For infections caused by Gram-negative bacilli, the preferred regimens are Ciprofloxacin at 750 mg orally twice daily or Levofloxacin at 750 mg orally once daily. 5. For diabetic foot osteomyelitis: The primary regimen includes an antibiotic dosed at 1.5–1 g IV every 6–8 hours, though this is not effective against MRSA. Alternative regimens include: 1. Levofloxacin at 750 mg IV or orally every 24 hours combined with Clindamycin at 150–300 mg orally four times daily. 2. Ciprofloxacin at 600–1200 mg/day IV every 6–12 hours combined with Clindamycin at 150–300 mg orally four times daily. 3. For more severe cases, Ciprofloxacin at 1200–2700 mg IV every 6–12 hours combined with Clindamycin at 150–300 mg orally four times daily. For patients at high risk for MRSA, the preferred regimens include: 1. Linezolid at 600 mg IV or orally every 12 hours. 2. Daptomycin at 4 mg/kg IV every 24 hours. 3. Vancomycin at 15–20 mg/kg IV every 8–12 hours, with a target trough level of 10–20 mg/L.
